comparisons.peer_summary: AMD utilizes TSMC, GLOBALFOUNDRIES, UMC, and Samsung for wafer production and IC manufacturing for its HPC, FPGA, and Adaptive SoC products, specifically noting GF's role for 12 nm and 14 nm nodes and multiple foundries for programmable logic devices.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD disclose their manufacturing capacity strategies, but Intel owns and expands its own fabrication facilities while AMD relies entirely on third-party foundries. Intel explicitly details its 'shell ahead' capacity expansion in Arizona, Ireland, and Ohio, whereas AMD lists its external partners (TSMC, GF, UMC, Samsung) for wafer production. This highlights the fundamental difference between Intel's integrated model and AMD's fabless supply chain management.

sentences.text: We refer to this strategy as "shell ahead." As a result of the supply shocks driven by the Covid-19 pandemic and the projected growth of our products businesses, we set out to expand our capacity network beyond our existing wafer production facilities in Oregon (mostly utilized for technology development and early production on new nodes), Arizona, Ireland, and Israel to meet this demand and get to "shell ahead" status.

We are in the later stages of an expansion of our wafer fabrication facilities in Ireland for our Intel 4 and Intel 3 process nodes and undertaking a significant expansion of our Arizona facility for our upcoming Intel 18A process node.

We utilize Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited (TSMC) for the production of wafers for our HPC, FPGA and Adaptive SoC products and GLOBALFOUNDRIES Inc. (GF), with respect to wafer purchases for our HPC products at the 12 nm and 14 nm technology nodes.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company has a long history of operating in Asia, where it manufactures and sources the majority of its products and materials, and stores the majority of its product inventory in a warehouse in Malaysia.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose significant manufacturing and sourcing presence in Asia, specifically Malaysia. Intel mentions expanding assembly/test facilities in Malaysia (though plans were reduced), while Broadcom states it stores the majority of its product inventory in a warehouse in Malaysia and sources the majority of products there. This shared geographic focus in Malaysia contrasts with Intel's heavy domestic US expansion efforts in Arizona and Ohio.

sentences.text: We are expanding our facilities in New Mexico and Malaysia, though we recently reduced the extent of the expansion plans for Malaysia.
We store the majority of our product inventory in our warehouse in Malaysia and our presence in Asia places us in close proximity to many of our customers' manufacturing facilities.

comparisons.peer_topic: US capacity expansion and supply chain construction risks
comparisons.peer_summary: Expanding US production faces challenges due to labor shortages, skilled subcontractor availability, and intense competition for construction talent, potentially causing delays and cost increases.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron disclose risks associated with constructing new semiconductor fabrication facilities in the United States. Intel cites slowed completion of its Ohio facility due to reassessed demand, while Micron cites potential delays and cost increases due to labor shortages and competition for construction talent in the US. Both acknowledge the capital intensity and complexity of US fab construction.

Semiconductor fabs are complex, capital-intensive projects and require specialized knowledge, expertise, experience, and skill sets to construct and operate.

Additionally, difficulties in obtaining labor, skilled sub-contractors and other service providers or other resources could result in delays in completion of our construction projects and cost increases, including costs to operate these facilities.

comparisons.peer_topic: Fabless manufacturing strategy and supplier responsibilities
comparisons.peer_summary: The company utilizes a fabless strategy, partnering with suppliers for wafer fabrication, assembly, testing, and packaging, while suppliers handle the procurement of most raw materials.
comparisons.comparison: This comparison contrasts Intel's asset-heavy manufacturing expansion with Nvidia's asset-light fabless strategy. Intel describes building its own 'wafer production facility in Ohio' and expanding Arizona, whereas Nvidia explicitly states it 'avoids many of the significant costs and risks associated with owning and operating manufacturing operations' by using a fabless strategy with third-party suppliers for all phases including wafer fabrication.

sentences.text: We are building a new wafer production facility in Ohio and have plans for an additional new wafer production facility in Germany, but have slowed the completion of the Ohio facility and put the plans for the facility in Germany on hold as we have reassessed demand and our "shell ahead" status and sought to limit our capital expenditures given recent financial results.

We utilize a fabless and contracting manufacturing strategy, whereby we employ and partner with key suppliers for all phases of the manufacturing process, including wafer fabrication, assembly, testing, and packaging.
Additionally, we can avoid many of the significant costs and risks associated with owning and operating manufacturing operations.
